title: assimilateSkill clobbers sibling-pack owner edges — the same defect TASK-200 fixed, in the data-loss direction
description:
Found by TASK-200's reviewer, which went looking for siblings of the defect it was reviewing rather than stopping at the one in scope.

**The defect.** `src/assimilate.js:586-599` — `assimilateSkill` writes `owners: []` and then calls `addOwner(lock, id, pack)`. This is character-for-character the pattern TASK-200 just removed from `executeInstall`: re-assimilating a resource id that another pack already owns **silently drops the sibling's edge**.

**Why this one is worse than TASK-200's.** TASK-200's residual fails toward *retention* — an edge survives that should have gone, and a human can clear it. This one fails toward *deletion*: once pack A's edge is dropped, pack A's resource looks unowned, and the assimilating pack's later remove deletes a resource pack A still wants. That is precisely the failure mode TASK-200's own description names, and it is unrecoverable.

**Not introduced by TASK-200** — it predates that ticket and sits outside `executeInstall`'s scope, which is why it was correctly not treated as a blocker there.

**Live-ness.** The same reasoning that made TASK-200's defect latent applies: no multi-owner entries exist in any lockfile today, and the two built-in packs (`design-power`, `watch`) declare disjoint resources. **Verify this independently rather than inheriting the claim** — assimilation is a human-gated path that adopts third-party skills, so the population of resource ids it can touch is not bounded by the built-in descriptors the way the reconciler's is. A consumer who assimilates a skill whose id collides with a pack-owned one is the realistic trigger.

**The fix is almost certainly TASK-200's fix applied here** — seed from the prior entry's owners and union, rather than reset. Read TASK-200's closing comment for the reasoning it recorded, and prefer consistency with it over inventing a second approach; two divergent implementations of the same invariant is its own defect class this repo has hit before.

**Check for further instances while you are here.** TASK-200's reviewer found this one by grepping for the pattern; a third may exist. Search every writer of `owners` across `src/` and report what you find, even if you fix only this one.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first reproduces the clobber through the real assimilate path: a resource already owned by pack A is re-assimilated, and pack A's owner edge disappears. Capture the red-run output verbatim.
Sibling-pack owner edges survive assimilateSkill, matching the invariant TASK-200 established for executeInstall.
The downstream consequence is proven, not just the field: after the re-assimilation, a resource still owned by pack A is not removable as an orphan - the same shape as TASK-200's AC3 spec.
Every writer of owners[] across src/ is surveyed and the result reported, so a third instance is either fixed or explicitly recorded as absent.
The approach is consistent with TASK-200's preserve-and-union rather than a second divergent implementation; if a different approach is genuinely needed here, state why in the closing comment.

Live-ness is verified independently rather than inherited: report whether any current lockfile or built-in pack can actually reach this, given assimilation adopts third-party ids outside the built-in descriptors' range.
npm run test:all is green; dist bundles rebuilt and committed if bundled source changes, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
**APPROVE** — fix round `d2c0836..b5a8102`, FULL depth, tier `tdd`. **0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM outstanding / 3 LOW closed.** Round 1's APPROVE (`d61c165..15e41f4`) is intact and strengthened.

**Gate:** `test:since -- d2c0836` 4 files / 91 passed, no zero-selection marker ⬛ `npm test` 89 files / 1180 passed, 2 skipped ⬛ `test:all` **190 passed | 1 skipped (191 files), 2201 passed | 4 skipped, 0 failed** ⬛ named + expanded e2e 6 files / 101 passed including all-8-bundle dist-parity ⬛ `check:calibration` clean. Count variance vs round 1 (189/2197) is the concurrent TASK-197 work plus this round's +1 spec; no failure named a TASK-203 file.

## The red-plant asymmetry — verified independently, not taken on trust

The reviewer rebuilt the plant itself from the shipped commit (`git show b5a8102:src/assimilate.js` with the second argument swapped `pack` → `id`, run from a scratchpad against the real `applyPlan`, zero repo mutation) and ran all three TASK-203 scenarios against both the planted and shipped modules:

```
=== RED-PLANT (2nd arg -> id) ===
  PASS  spec1 RED-LOCK (AC1/AC2)
  FAIL  spec2 AC2 (TASK-202 wiring)   <-- the new one
        -> expected ["design-power@0.1.0","third-party-assimilate@1.0.0"]
              got ["design-power@0.1.0","third-party-assimilate@0.9.0","third-party-assimilate@1.0.0"]
  PASS  spec3 AC3 (lock entry + live dir)

=== SHIPPED (b5a8102, 2nd arg -> pack) ===
  PASS  spec1    PASS  spec2    PASS  spec3
```

**The plant fails exactly one spec — the new one.** That asymmetry is the whole proof: the sensor isolates the wiring and nothing else masks it. The failure is a real assertion on real values (a stranded `third-party-assimilate@0.9.0` phantom edge), not a TypeError.

## The AC3 live-dir assertion has teeth

Checked that `expect(existsSync(liveDir)).toBe(true)` is not vacuously always-true, by running the same scenario against the pre-fix module:

```
PRE-FIX (d61c165):  existsSync(liveDir) -> false   FAIL (live dir DELETED)
SHIPPED (b5a8102):  existsSync(liveDir) -> true    PASS
```

`executeRemove`'s `rmSync(liveDir)` half is now genuinely exercised. **Both halves of the data-loss consequence — disk and lock — are locked.**

## What must NOT have changed — confirmed

- **The 3-line fix is byte-unchanged.** Filtering the round-over-round `src/assimilate.js` diff to non-comment lines yields `NO non-comment source lines changed`. This was a test-only round plus the comment collapse, exactly as scoped.
- **AC5 consistency holds.** `src/assimilate.js:599` → `dropStaleSameOwnerEdges(priorOwners, pack)` vs `src/pack-apply.js:489` → `dropStaleSameOwnerEdges(priorOwners, owner)`; the preceding `priorOwners` guard line is character-identical. One invariant, one implementation.
- **TASK-202 malformed-owner `null` contract unchanged** — both probes re-run, byte-identical to round 1: a malformed *prior* owner is preserved untouched, a malformed *current* owner is a no-op drop plus a plain union.
- **No scope creep into TASK-207.** The `required: hard → soft` downgrade and entry-provenance clobber are still present and untouched (probes still show `required: soft (was hard)`) — correct; that is TASK-207's to fix.
- **`dist/` correctly NOT rebuilt.** `b5a8102` touches no `dist/` file. Right call: esbuild strips comments, so a comment-only source edit changes no bundle bytes. dist-parity confirms all 8 still byte-match a fresh build.

## Comment collapse — nothing load-bearing lost

19 lines → 9. The call-site-specific paragraph survives intact (human-gated adoption of a possibly third-party `resourceId`; "a colliding resourceId is a real, reachable trigger, not a hypothetical one"). The `src/pack-descriptor.js`-doesn't-forbid-collisions grounding was dropped locally but is preserved verbatim at the canonical site the new comment points to (`src/pack-apply.js:476-479`). That is precisely what a pointer-collapse should do: one copy of the rationale at the canonical location, with the call-site-specific delta kept local.

## Findings

**HIGH: none. MEDIUM: none outstanding.** Both round-1 MEDIUMs are resolved or correctly re-homed — the unspecced wiring is **closed** (plant-verified asymmetric), and the entry-provenance / `required` clobber is **re-homed to TASK-207** and correctly untouched here.

**LOW (all closed or documentation-only):** the AC3 sensor LOW is closed (live dir materialized, assertion proven non-vacuous); the comment-volume LOW is closed; the AC6 survey under-count stands as a nit only — the hand-off listed 9 of the 10 resource ids `packs/design-power/descriptor.json` declares, omitting `21st-dev-magic`. The conclusion is unaffected and correct.

**New-test budget:** 3 TASK-203 specs, each proven load-bearing by a *distinct* failure mode — spec1 catches the sibling-edge clobber, spec2 uniquely catches the wiring, spec3 uniquely catches the on-disk half. No redundancy; the new spec reuses the existing `seedPriorLockEntry` helper rather than adding a second one. **Minimalism: net source lines went DOWN this round.**

**Verdict: APPROVE.** Both findings closed with sensors verified non-vacuous by independent red-planting rather than by reading the developer's report.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**CLOSED on a green independent review.** Review depth **FULL**; rubric inputs: the diff touches packaging/dist (`dist/pack-ctl.cjs`) and core `tdd`-tier logic in `src/assimilate.js` — the third-party skill adoption path, a security-relevant trust boundary. Either input forces FULL regardless of line count (round 1 was ~4 files; the fix round 2 files, 53+/20-).

Commits `15e41f4` (fix + tests) and `b5a8102` (sensor hardening). Tier `tdd`, single developer spawn per round. **Note the commit graph is interleaved with TASK-197** — `d61c165` (197 r1), `15e41f4` (203 r1), `d2c0836` (197 r2), `b5a8102` (203 r2) — so this ticket's diff is **non-contiguous** and no single range describes it.

## The defect closed

`src/assimilate.js` wrote `owners: []` then called `addOwner` — character-for-character the pattern TASK-200 removed from `executeInstall`. Re-assimilating a resource id another pack already owns silently dropped the sibling's edge. **This failed toward deletion, not retention:** pack A's resource then looked unowned, and the assimilating pack's later remove deleted a resource pack A still wanted. Unrecoverable, and strictly worse than TASK-200's own residual.

The fix is 3 lines and reuses the existing machinery rather than inventing a second implementation — seed from the prior entry's owners, run through TASK-202's `dropStaleSameOwnerEdges`, let `addOwner` union. The reviewer diffed the two call sites and confirmed `src/assimilate.js:599` and `src/pack-apply.js:489` are textually identical apart from the owner variable name, with the preceding guard line character-identical. **One invariant, one implementation** — which is the whole point of AC5, since two divergent implementations of one invariant is a defect class this repo has already been bitten by.

## Why this ticket went a second round even though round 1 was an APPROVE

The reviewer approved round 1 but flagged that **the fix's wiring was unspecced**: with prior owners `['design-power@0.1.0']` and `pack = 'third-party-assimilate@1.0.0'`, `dropStaleSameOwnerEdges` is a no-op — so both round-1 tests passed identically whether the second argument was `pack`, `id`, or omitted entirely. The implementation was verified correct by probe, so this was a sensor gap, not a live defect.

**Sending it back was the right call rather than accepting the APPROVE as-is.** An unpinned fix on a data-loss path in a trust-boundary module is exactly how this class recurs, and the cost was one test. The proof it now works is the **asymmetry**: with the second argument planted back to `id`, exactly one spec fails — the new one — while the other two stay green. Had all three gone red, the test would not have been isolating the wiring at all. The reviewer rebuilt that plant itself from the shipped commit rather than trusting the developer's report.

The AC3 sensor was also strengthened: it had proven the downstream consequence only through the lock entry, never materializing a live directory, so `executeRemove`'s `rmSync(liveDir)` half went unexercised. A live dir is now materialized and its survival asserted — and proven non-vacuous (pre-fix: `existsSync -> false`, the dir really is deleted). Both halves of the data-loss consequence, disk and lock, are now locked.

## AC6 live-ness — verified, not inherited

The ticket asked for independent verification rather than inheriting TASK-200's latency claim, and that mattered. Confirmed: `integrations.lock.json` holds 2 entries with exactly one owner each, no multi-owner entries; the two built-in packs declare disjoint resource ids. **But that disjointness does not bound assimilation's input space** — `resourceId` on this path is human-supplied and constrained by no descriptor, so a consumer assimilating any third-party skill whose id collides is a real, unbounded trigger. The developer reached that conclusion rather than repeating the inherited one.

(Minor, recorded for accuracy: the survey listed 9 of the 10 resource ids `packs/design-power/descriptor.json` declares, omitting `21st-dev-magic`. The conclusion is unaffected.)

## AC4 survey result

Every writer of `owners[]` in `src/`, confirmed by the reviewer's own grep rather than the developer's list: `integrations-lock.js` (`addOwner`/`dropOwner`), `pack-apply.js` (`executeInstall`, fixed by TASK-200/202), `assimilate.js` (fixed here). `pack-reconcile.js:231` is a **read**, not a writer, and `assimilate.js:635` is a read for the return payload — now covered by AC1's `expect(result.owners).toEqual(entry.owners)`. **No third writer instance exists.** The chain that began at TASK-200 is complete.

## Follow-up minted: TASK-207

The reviewer looked past its own scope and found that a colliding `resourceId` still clobbers the sibling pack's entry **provenance** (`origin`, `pin`) and downgrades its `required: 'hard'` to `'soft'` — and `required: 'hard'` is a removal brake at `src/pack-reconcile.js:233`. That re-opens a removal path in the same direction this ticket closes, one level up through a different field. Pre-existing, outside this ticket's scope, and deliberately left untouched (the reviewer verified no scope creep: probes still show `required: soft (was hard)`).

`dist/pack-ctl.cjs` was rebuilt and committed at `15e41f4`; the fix round correctly did **not** rebuild it, since esbuild strips comments and a comment-only edit changes no bundle bytes. dist-parity byte-matches all 8 bundles. Net source lines went **down** in the second round.
